before: A switch expression chooses a result from arms written pattern => result. Its input appears before switch.
The first matching arm wins. Constant patterns such as 1 match that exact value.
The discard pattern _ matches any remaining input. Put it last so unmatched values have an intentional result.
A switch expression produces a value. A switch statement with case and break is a related control-flow form, but is not used in this example.
Expected behavior from this example: Write. This expected result is a reasoned prediction until a compiler test is recorded.

Optional local transfer task: Add a third menu choice and predict both that choice and an unknown input. Keep the fallback last. You may trace it on paper if no C# toolchain is installed; reading completion does not certify a run.
after: A switch expression looks at a value and chooses a result. Here, it looks at the menu number.
Each choice has a pattern on the left of => and a result on the right. A number pattern matches that exact number.
C# checks the choices from top to bottom. It uses the first one that matches.
The _ pattern matches anything left over. Put it last so an unknown menu number gets a helpful result.
menu is 2, so the result is Write. The program saves that text in action and prints it.
This switch produces a value that can be saved or passed to other code. A switch statement is a related form that uses case labels to choose which statements to run.
